chapters.body:
# Snapshot

## What the company is

Sivers Semiconductors AB (ticker: SIVE.ST; OTC US: SIVEF) was a Swedish holding company with two operating subsidiaries that shared little beyond a parent, a balance sheet and a listing. **Sivers Wireless AB** made millimetre-wave beamformers, phased-array ICs and antenna modules for SATCOM, 5G/6G and defence. **Sivers Photonics Ltd.** designed custom indium-phosphide distributed-feedback lasers and laser arrays for silicon-photonics, sensing and, increasingly, external light-source architectures aimed at AI datacenters. The wireless side had named institutional customers including the [European Space Agency](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-awarded-european-space-agency-contract-for-next-generation-satcom-beamforming-ics/) and [Intelsat](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-wins-intelsat-satcom-digitizer-development-program-award/); the photonics side was being marketed as an upstream supplier to co-packaged-optics ecosystems rather than to hyperscalers directly. Management was simultaneously evaluating a potential [Nasdaq New York dual listing](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-ab-evaluates-a-potential-dual-listing-of-its-shares-on-the-nasdaq-new-york/).

At the 22 May 2026 close of SEK 72.90 on the company's [share-price widget](https://widget.datablocks.se/api/rose/widgets/stock-chart?token=01434696-043a-4b12-8609-959b0f82e6a0&lang=en), and using the AGM notice's 14 May 2026 ordinary-share count net of treasury stock, Sivers carried an equity value of roughly SEK 22.2 billion. The AGM notice said the company had 305,154,751 ordinary shares outstanding, of which it held 896,214 in treasury; the remaining 14,798,821 series C shares carried reduced voting rights and were treasury-held. [AGM notice](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/notice-to-attend-the-annual-general-meeting-of-sivers-semiconductors-ab-publ-6/)

## Seventy-five years, three acts

Founded in 1951 by engineer Carl von Sivers as Sivers Lab AB, the business began as a specialist microwave-component manufacturer. Philips Sweden absorbed it in 1960; a 1983 merger with IMA AB created Sivers IMA; a 1990 management buyout restored independence. The modern group was created by two acquisitions: CST Global in 2017, which became Sivers Photonics, and MixComm in 2022, which expanded the US millimetre-wave operation. Chapter 2 traces the full corporate arc. [Sivers history](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/company-2/history/)

## The management team that mattered for the US listing

Vickram Vathulya was appointed President and CEO on 19 August 2024. Sivers said he brought more than 25 years of semiconductor experience from NXP, Maxim and, most recently, Nuvotronics. In September 2024 the board also approved a directed issue of 1,524,584 ordinary shares to him and proposed 2,000,000 employee stock options for the chief executive, conditional on his purchase or subscription of at least 2,000,000 ordinary shares in the company, capped at USD 1 million. [CEO appointment](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-appoints-vickram-vathulya-as-new-president-ceo/), [CEO directed issue and incentive plan](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/the-board-of-directors-in-sivers-semiconductors-resolves-on-a-directed-share-issue-to-the-ceo-and-proposes-an-incentive-program-for-the-groups-employees/)

Bami Bastani joined as [strategic adviser](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/semiconductor-industry-veteran-bami-bastani-joins-sivers-semiconductors-as-strategic-advisor/) in August 2023 and, by February 2024, had been appointed US executive chairman and nominated as chairman of the Swedish parent. Sivers described him as having more than 42 years of semiconductor-industry experience, including senior roles at GlobalFoundries and prior chief executive turns at ANADIGICS, Trident Microsystems and Meru Networks. [Bastani chairman appointment](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/dr-bami-bastani-is-nominated-as-the-chairman-of-the-board-of-directors-of-sivers-semiconductors-ab-and-is-appointed-executive-chairman-of-sivers-semiconductors-inc/)

## FY2025: growth, but deeper losses after the accounting uplift

The full-year 2025 results, published on 13 May 2026, were restated on a PCAOB-aligned basis as part of the company's preparation for a possible US listing.

| Metric | Swedish K3 (original) | PCAOB-restated |
|---|---|---|
| Net sales (SEK M) | 304.1 | 306.6 |
| EBIT (SEK M) | −141.3 | −177.8 |
| Net loss (SEK M) | −186.5 | −222.6 |
| EPS (SEK) | −0.69 | −0.81 |
| Equity per share (SEK) | 3.46 | 3.05 |

Revenue grew 40 per cent year on year to SEK 306.6 million on the restated basis, while the sales pipeline rose 64 per cent during 2025 to USD 453 million. Cash and cash equivalents at year-end were SEK 43.5 million. The company then refinanced its debt with a [USD 17 million Bootstrap Europe facility](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-refinances-group-debt-facilities-with-bootstrap-europe-to-strengthen-capital-structure/) and, on 19 May 2026, announced a [USD 6.6 million Year 2 NEMC award](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/microelectronics-commons-strengthens-commitment-to-sivers-semiconductors-with-year-2-funding/). [2025 annual report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/), [Q4 2025 interim report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Sivers-Interim-report-Q425_Final.pdf)

## The question the rest of this report answers

Was Sivers becoming a genuine upstream chokepoint for co-packaged optics, or was the market capitalisation already discounting revenue that still sat in the prototype-and-qualification stage? The first near-term governance test was the 15 June 2026 AGM, where shareholders were asked to approve a 15 per cent issuance mandate, elect a reshaped five-member board and give the company explicit flexibility to support a potential Nasdaq New York process. [AGM notice](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/notice-to-attend-the-annual-general-meeting-of-sivers-semiconductors-ab-publ-6/)

chapters.title: From Sivers Lab to Sivers Photonics — 75 years
chapters.body:
# From Sivers Lab to Sivers Photonics — 75 years

## A passive-microwave shop in Stockholm, 1951

Carl von Sivers founded Sivers Lab AB in Sweden in 1951 to make passive microwave components — slotted-line VSWR detectors and the instrumentation that surrounds them. It was artisanal, specialized work, serving defence laboratories and university physics departments across Scandinavia. Nine years later, in 1960, Philips Sweden absorbed the company, and Sivers Lab effectively disappeared into a multinational for what would prove to be a long, under-documented interval.

The thread re-emerges in 1983, when Philips merged Sivers Lab with IMA AB — a Stockholm-based maker of microwave components and oscillators for radar applications, founded in 1975 — to create Sivers IMA, a producer of magnetically tunable filters and oscillators using yttrium-iron-garnet (YIG) technology. Seven years later, in 1990, the management bought the company out of Philips through a vehicle called SI Holding AB, restoring it as an independent supplier ([Sivers history page](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/company-2/history/)). The 1990s saw a divestment of high-power microwave operations and the acquisition of the Swedish filter maker Lyscom; the 2000s and early 2010s brought low-phase-noise products, ultra-wideband VCOs, and the proprietary millimetre-wave converters that would eventually anchor the wireless subsidiary. Sivers IMA Holding AB began trading on Nasdaq First North Stockholm on 30 November 2017, moving to the main Nasdaq Stockholm board on 10 June 2021.

## The foundational move: CST Global, 2017

Everything that makes Sivers interesting to investors today traces back to a single acquisition. In 2017, Sivers IMA Holding bought [CST Global](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/), a Scottish manufacturer of III-V photonic devices with its own R&D facility and clean-room fabrication capacity outside Glasgow. CST Global supplied photonic components in wafer, coated bar, chip device, and die-on-tape formats — bespoke, low-volume, high-specification work for customers who could not or would not go to the large Asian foundries.

The renamed subsidiary, Sivers Photonics Ltd., gave the group something no amount of microwave-component iteration could have produced: a captive, western-domiciled source of indium phosphide distributed-feedback (InP DFB) lasers. DFB lasers at specific C-band wavelengths (1530–1565 nm) are the light engines inside the transceiver modules that carry data through fibre. In 2017, that was a niche. By 2025 it was a chokepoint.

Two years after the CST deal closed, Sivers Photonics and imec announced a collaboration to integrate C-band InP DFB laser arrays directly onto imec's silicon photonics platform. The work pointed squarely toward the co-packaged optics architecture that hyperscalers would not start seriously deploying for another five years.

## Wireless expansion and the rebrand

In 2022, the group acquired MixComm, a US-based millimetre-wave startup, bolting it into the Sivers Wireless AB subsidiary alongside the legacy beamformer and phased-array business. MixComm brought additional customers in 5G fixed wireless, SATCOM, and defence. Two years earlier, in 2020, the parent had renamed itself Sivers Semiconductors AB and consolidated the operating entities under their current names — Sivers Wireless AB (mmWave RF) and Sivers Photonics Ltd. (DFB lasers).

## The American turn

The signals pointing toward a US capital-markets strategy began appearing in mid-2023. In August of that year, Bami Bastani joined the board as a Strategic Advisor. By February 2024 he was Executive Chairman of Sivers Inc. and Chairman of Sivers AB. Six months later, in August 2024, Vickram Vathulya replaced Anders Storm as CEO. (Chapter 6 carries the leadership detail in full.)

## 2025–26: the accounting signal

On 13 May 2026, the group published its [2025 Annual Report with PCAOB-restated financials](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/), explicitly framed as preparation for a potential Nasdaq New York dual listing. The mechanics of the restatement are dissected in Chapter 4.

A $6.6 million NEMC Year 2 grant from the US Department of Defense, announced on 19 May 2026, reinforced the American vector. An AGM scheduled for June 2026 carries a 15% dilution authority vote and a board reshuffle suggesting the capital structure is still being shaped for whatever the dual-listing roadshow requires.

---

Sivers spent roughly 65 years as a passive-microwave shop before two acquisitions in five years turned it into what its current management is betting will prove to be a laser chokepoint in the AI optical-interconnect supply chain. The pace of transformation is the story.

chapters.title: Two subsidiaries, two supply chains

# Two subsidiaries, two supply chains

## One competency, two markets

The two wholly owned subsidiaries — Sivers Wireless AB in Stockholm and Sivers Photonics Ltd. in Glasgow — served structurally different end-markets while sharing the same core materials competence: building precision radio-frequency and photonic components from compound III-V semiconductors, principally indium phosphide and gallium arsenide. That common substrate was the technological logic for keeping them under one listed parent.

Commercially, though, they behaved very differently. Wireless sold into long-cycle institutional procurement — satellite operators, space agencies, telecom and defence programmes. Photonics sold into design cycles tied to AI optical interconnects, sensing and custom silicon-photonics applications, where early design wins could become much larger production positions if customer qualification succeeded.

## Sivers Wireless AB: the institutional floor

The wireless subsidiary produced millimetre-wave beamformers, phased-array ICs, digitizers and antenna modules for four principal application groups: SATCOM, fixed wireless access, 5G/6G infrastructure, and defence and aerospace.

The sovereignty angle was not just marketing language. In its December 2025 ESA release, Sivers described itself as the only EU-based commercial provider of mmWave beamforming ICs for SATCOM and 5G. The company backed that positioning with named programmes: a new [European Space Agency beamforming-IC contract](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-awarded-european-space-agency-contract-for-next-generation-satcom-beamforming-ics/), an [Intelsat digitizer development award](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-wins-intelsat-satcom-digitizer-development-program-award/), and CHIPS Act-funded/NEMC-backed US defence work that was extended again in May 2026. [ESA contract](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-awarded-european-space-agency-contract-for-next-generation-satcom-beamforming-ics/), [Intelsat contract](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-wins-intelsat-satcom-digitizer-development-program-award/), [NEMC Year 2 funding](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/microelectronics-commons-strengthens-commitment-to-sivers-semiconductors-with-year-2-funding/)

Wireless was therefore not merely the legacy business. It was the division that gave the group a base of contracted development programmes, institutional reference customers and a defensible role in Western SATCOM and defence supply chains.

## Sivers Photonics Ltd.: the CPO thesis

Sivers Photonics made high-power indium-phosphide DFB lasers, laser arrays and optical amplifiers, and it was increasingly trying to turn those devices into the laser layer inside external light-source architectures for AI interconnects. The technical argument was straightforward: silicon photonics still needed an external indium-phosphide light source, and the higher the bandwidth target, the more painful it became to manage wavelength stability, thermal load and serviceability inside the package itself.

That was why Sivers kept turning up in external-light-source announcements rather than in finished switch or GPU products. Its late-2025 and early-2026 announcements with POET, O-Net and Enablence all revolved around feeding laser arrays into someone else's optical engine, interposer or module. Chapters 7 and 8 examine whether that layer was narrow enough to support chokepoint economics.

## The LiDAR wildcard

Photonics was not only an AI-datacenter story. On 11 March 2026, Sivers disclosed that an unnamed strategic LiDAR customer had incorporated Sivers technology across its platforms and was targeting a production ramp from Q4 2026 for automotive and industrial uses. Sivers said it expected to supply both lasers and optical amplifiers, with cumulative revenue potential of USD 53 million to USD 138 million across the customer's product lifecycle. The customer remained unnamed as of the frozen date. [LiDAR customer release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/strategic-lidar-customer-ramps-remote-sensing-production-with-sivers-semiconductors-technology/)

## The financial picture — less opaque after the restatement

The annual report did, in fact, publish a cleaner divisional split than the earlier dossier suggested. Restated FY2025 net sales were SEK 213.1 million for Wireless and SEK 93.4 million for Photonics. In the product mix note, hardware revenue totalled SEK 127.2 million, of which SEK 93.4 million came from Photonics and SEK 33.8 million from Wireless, after the company reclassified Photonics NRE revenue into hardware revenue. That mattered because it showed the AI-photonics narrative was driving valuation long before photonics had overtaken wireless in reported revenue. [2025 annual report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/)

## The segment-level verdict

Wireless was the historical floor and the institutional credibility anchor. Photonics was the option value: the business tied to POET, Ayar Labs, O-Net/Enablence and the unnamed LiDAR customer, and the division most exposed to the USD 453 million pipeline that management disclosed in the February 2026 year-end report. Wireless financed time; photonics had to justify the multiple. [Q4 2025 interim report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Sivers-Interim-report-Q425_Final.pdf)

# Two sets of books — and what the restatement actually means

## The restatement in plain language

On 13 May 2026, Sivers Semiconductors published its 2025 Annual Report almost three months after preliminary year-end numbers had already been released. The delay was deliberate. The company said it had uplifted its 2024 and 2025 accounts to PCAOB standards as preparation for a potential US listing, and the differences were material. FY2025 EBIT worsened by SEK 36.5 million, net loss deepened by SEK 36.1 million, and equity fell by SEK 127.0 million versus the earlier Swedish K3 presentation. [2025 annual report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/)

Two sets of books therefore existed at the snapshot date. Swedish K3 was the statutory history; the PCAOB-restated numbers were the set management wanted investors to use when comparing Sivers with US-listed peers.

| Metric | As reported (K3) | PCAOB-restated | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Net sales (SEK M) | 304.1 | 306.6 | +2.5 |
| EBIT (SEK M) | −141.3 | −177.8 | −36.5 |
| Net result (SEK M) | −186.5 | −222.6 | −36.1 |
| EPS (SEK) | −0.69 | −0.81 | −0.12 |
| Equity (SEK M) | 1,076.8 | 949.8 | −127.0 |
| Equity/share (SEK) | 3.46 | 3.05 | −0.41 |

Revenue, notably, edged upward under PCAOB rather than downward. That did not make the uplift benign; it simply meant revenue was being re-timed across periods, with FY2024 weakened and FY2025 flattered at the margin by the new recognition framework.

## The five levers — and which one cut deepest

The company disclosed five restatement drivers. The largest analytical issue was the impairment of previously capitalised development expenditure. Swedish K3 had allowed Sivers to carry more development spend as an asset; the PCAOB framework pushed more of that spend through the income statement and trimmed book equity.

Revenue recognition was the second major lever. Restated FY2024 revenue fell to SEK 219.2 million from SEK 243.7 million, while the FY2024 net loss widened to SEK 183.9 million from SEK 116.3 million. Investors who had used the original FY2024 base had been relying on a meaningfully more generous starting point. [2025 annual report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/)

Inventory adjustments, fair-value changes on share-based compensation and the switch from classification by nature to classification by function completed the uplift. The last of those did not change total losses, but it did recast the statements into a format that US equity investors would recognise more readily.

## What the operating trajectory looked like after the uplift

Even on the more conservative basis, the 2025 operating direction was real. Restated net sales rose 40 per cent year on year to SEK 306.6 million. Wireless revenue increased to SEK 213.1 million from SEK 139.2 million, while Photonics revenue rose to SEK 93.4 million from SEK 80.1 million. Net cash flow from operating activities before changes in working capital was negative SEK 64.8 million, so the company was still burning cash even as revenue accelerated. [2025 annual report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/)

The February 2026 year-end report had already shown the commercial momentum that investors cared about: Q4 net sales of SEK 80.7 million, reported growth of 5 per cent, constant-currency growth of 17 per cent, and a year-end pipeline of USD 453 million. The annual report did not invalidate that demand narrative; it put harsher accounting around it. [Q4 2025 interim report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Sivers-Interim-report-Q425_Final.pdf)

## Capital structure: the cost of survival

The financing history remained central because the restated accounts still left Sivers with little margin for error. Year-end cash and cash equivalents were SEK 43.5 million. In September 2025 the company completed a [directed share issue of SEK 95 million](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-has-completed-a-directed-share-issue-of-approximately-sek-95-million/) by selling 25,675,675 new ordinary shares at SEK 3.70, lifting total shares to 311,333,572. On 24 February 2026 it refinanced all external debt with Bootstrap Europe through a USD 5 million term loan bearing 12 per cent interest and a USD 12 million convertible loan bearing 10.85 per cent interest, convertible at SEK 4.77 and representing up to 22,847,044 new ordinary shares. [Bootstrap refinancing](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-refinances-group-debt-facilities-with-bootstrap-europe-to-strengthen-capital-structure/)

By 14 May 2026, after the April/May directed issue approved at the EGM, the AGM notice showed 319,953,572 shares outstanding in total, including 305,154,751 ordinary shares. The same AGM notice asked shareholders to authorise issues of up to 53,844,956 additional ordinary shares — about 15 per cent dilution relative to the current ordinary-share count — and said that mandate could also be used to facilitate a Nasdaq New York listing. [AGM notice](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/notice-to-attend-the-annual-general-meeting-of-sivers-semiconductors-ab-publ-6/), [EGM bulletin](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/bulletin-from-the-extraordinary-general-meeting-in-sivers-semiconductors-ab-publ-on-11-may-2026/)

## The valuation arithmetic

At SEK 72.90 on 22 May 2026, and using the ordinary-share count net of treasury stock disclosed in the AGM notice, the equity market was valuing Sivers at about SEK 22.2 billion. Against FY2025 restated revenue of SEK 306.6 million, that equated to roughly 72 times trailing sales. Whatever else investors believed, they were not capitalising the company on present-day earnings power. [Share-price widget](https://widget.datablocks.se/api/rose/widgets/stock-chart?token=01434696-043a-4b12-8609-959b0f82e6a0&lang=en), [AGM notice](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/notice-to-attend-the-annual-general-meeting-of-sivers-semiconductors-ab-publ-6/), [2025 annual report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/)

## The frame for what followed

The PCAOB uplift answered one question cleanly: the conservative baseline for analysis was the restated one. It also sharpened a second question. If the cleaner accounting, the 15 per cent issuance request, the Bootstrap financing and the USD 453 million pipeline were all part of the same transition into a US-facing equity story, then the next stage had to be shipment and cash generation rather than additional narrative. The restatement did not break the thesis; it made the cost of missing the thesis much easier to see.

# The five quarters that built the rally

The move was not subtle. From the five-year low of SEK 1.80 on 20 November 2024 to the close of SEK 72.90 on 22 May 2026, Sivers' shares rose a little more than 40-fold on the company's own share-price history. Five quarters explained most of that rerating. [Share-price widget](https://widget.datablocks.se/api/rose/widgets/stock-chart?token=01434696-043a-4b12-8609-959b0f82e6a0&lang=en)

## August 2024: the handover

The first step was managerial rather than financial. Vickram Vathulya took over as chief executive on 19 August 2024, replacing Anders Storm. The appointment introduced a management team that was far more overtly aligned with US semiconductor capital markets and with the co-packaged-optics narrative that later dominated the stock. [CEO appointment](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-appoints-vickram-vathulya-as-new-president-ceo/)

## H1 2025: contracts first, rerating later

The first half of 2025 built the factual scaffolding for the later move. In January, Sivers signed the [Intelsat digitizer programme](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-wins-intelsat-satcom-digitizer-development-program-award/) and the [NEMC CHIPS Act contracts](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-signs-chips-act-contracts-with-the-northeast-microelectronics-coalition-hub/). In April it announced an [OEM partnership with O-Net](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-announces-strategic-oem-partnership-with-o-net-technologies-to-deliver-next-generation-external-laser-sources-for-co-packaged-optics/). In May it reported Q1 2025 revenue of SEK 78.5 million, up 40 per cent year on year. None of that yet proved a photonics production ramp, but it broadened the list of named counterparties investors could anchor to. [Q1 2025 report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-ab-publ-publishes-interim-report-q1-january-march-2025/)

## September-November 2025: the POET anchor

The inflection point came in late 2025. On 29 September 2025, POET Technologies said it had entered a strategic collaboration with Sivers to develop external light-source modules for co-packaged optics and next-generation AI infrastructure. On 6 November, Sivers added its own more detailed framing, saying prototypes were expected in the first half of 2026 and production readiness by the end of 2026. That pair of releases gave the market something more tangible than a generic AI-photonics slogan: a named partner, a specific architecture and a timetable. [POET collaboration announcement](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-sivers-semiconductors-collaborate-on-external-light-sources-for-co-packaged-optics-and-next-generation-ai-market), [Sivers follow-up release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-partners-with-poet-technologies-to-deliver-innovative-light-engines-and-strengthen-serviceable-market-offerings-in-next-gen-ai-infrastructure/)

Ayar Labs reinforced that story rather than replacing it. Sivers had already been demonstrating laser arrays with Ayar's SuperNova platform and, in July 2023, disclosed a new USD 1 million Ayar order tied to light-source technology for generative AI. By late 2025, investors had enough named CPO-adjacent relationships to start treating Sivers as an upstream AI-optics option. [Ayar order](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-photonics-receives-new-order-worth-1m-from-ayar-labs-for-light-source-technology-to-support-the-growth-of-generative-ai/)

## February 2026: the preliminary read and the refinancing

On 24 February 2026, Sivers refinanced all external debt through Bootstrap Europe. Two days later, the company published the Q4 2025 report: Q4 net sales of SEK 80.7 million, annual net sales of SEK 304.1 million on the pre-restatement basis, product revenue of SEK 21.3 million in Q4 and a year-end pipeline of USD 453 million. The financing bought time; the year-end report kept the growth narrative intact. [Bootstrap refinancing](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-refinances-group-debt-facilities-with-bootstrap-europe-to-strengthen-capital-structure/), [Q4 2025 interim report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Sivers-Interim-report-Q425_Final.pdf)

## May 2026: the restatement that failed to break the tape

The annual report on 13 May 2026 should, on paper, have been a shock. It widened FY2025 EBIT and net loss materially under PCAOB-aligned reporting and pushed the Q1 2026 report from 20 May to 29 May. Yet the post-report share-price action was the opposite of capitulation: the stock closed at SEK 56.65 on 13 May and at SEK 72.90 on 22 May. Investors treated the accounting uplift as part of a listing process rather than as a repudiation of the commercial thesis. [2025 annual report release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/), [share-price widget](https://widget.datablocks.se/api/rose/widgets/stock-chart?token=01434696-043a-4b12-8609-959b0f82e6a0&lang=en)

## The test ahead

By the snapshot date, the rerating had been built on real management change, real counterparties, real contracts and a real pipeline. What still had not happened was the decisive thing the valuation was discounting: production-scale CPO revenue. Q1 2026 had been postponed to 29 May, the AGM was set for 15 June, POET prototype timing still pointed to 2026, and the LiDAR customer still pointed to a Q4 2026 ramp. The stock had already moved as if at least one of those schedules would hold.

# The team that is going to ring the Nasdaq bell

## The sequence was the message

The appointments did not arrive at random. Bami Bastani joined as strategic adviser in August 2023. In February 2024, Sivers said he had been appointed US executive chairman and nominated as chairman of the Swedish parent. Vickram Vathulya was then hired as chief executive effective 19 August 2024. By May 2026, the company had produced PCAOB-restated accounts and proposed a five-person board slate with two new directors and three departures. The pattern was hard to miss: Sivers was trying to make itself legible to US institutional capital. [Bastani adviser appointment](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/semiconductor-industry-veteran-bami-bastani-joins-sivers-semiconductors-as-strategic-advisor/), [Bastani chairman appointment](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/dr-bami-bastani-is-nominated-as-the-chairman-of-the-board-of-directors-of-sivers-semiconductors-ab-and-is-appointed-executive-chairman-of-sivers-semiconductors-inc/), [CEO appointment](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-appoints-vickram-vathulya-as-new-president-ceo/), [board nominations](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-welcomes-the-nomination-of-new-board-members-joakim-nideborn-and-helena-svancar/)

## Bastani: the operating chairman

Sivers described Bastani as bringing more than 42 years of semiconductor experience. The company cited senior roles at GlobalFoundries and prior chief-executive appointments at ANADIGICS, Trident Microsystems and Meru Networks. The present board page added that he had been elected to the board in 2024 and was also executive chairman of Sivers Semiconductors Inc. This was not a symbolic chairman brought in to dress up an investor deck; it was a US semiconductor operator with repeated public-company turnaround experience. [Bastani adviser appointment](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/semiconductor-industry-veteran-bami-bastani-joins-sivers-semiconductors-as-strategic-advisor/), [board page](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/investors/corporate-governance/board-of-directors-and-executive-management/)

## Vathulya: the CEO who was asked to buy stock

Vathulya's résumé was unusually tailored to the job Sivers now wanted done. The company said he held a PhD in electrical engineering from Lehigh and an MBA from Berkeley Haas, and had spent more than 25 years in semiconductors across NXP, Maxim and Nuvotronics. In September 2024, the board went further and approved a directed issue of 1,524,584 ordinary shares to him at SEK 4.536 per share, while also proposing 2,000,000 employee stock options for the CEO under programme P09. Those options were conditional on his purchase or subscription of at least 2,000,000 ordinary shares in Sivers, subject to a USD 1 million cap; the company said he had already bought 475,416 shares on-market by 13 September 2024. [CEO appointment](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-appoints-vickram-vathulya-as-new-president-ceo/), [CEO directed issue and incentive plan](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/the-board-of-directors-in-sivers-semiconductors-resolves-on-a-directed-share-issue-to-the-ceo-and-proposes-an-incentive-program-for-the-groups-employees/)

## Thomson and Raj: the pre-existing anchors

Todd Thomson had been on the board since 2021, before Bastani arrived. Sivers said he had previously served as Citigroup's CFO and as chief executive of Citi's Global Wealth Management division, with earlier experience at GE Capital, Bain and Booz Allen. If Bastani was the semiconductor operating chairman, Thomson was the capital-markets and balance-sheet counterweight. [board page](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/investors/corporate-governance/board-of-directors-and-executive-management/)

Karin Raj, elected in 2024, provided the technical and telecom counterbalance. Sivers identified her as CTO Europe at Nokia Networks, with prior roles at Acuvi, JonDeTech, Huawei Sweden and Ericsson. She was the board member whose background sat most directly inside the communications and deep-tech markets Sivers sold into. [board page](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/investors/corporate-governance/board-of-directors-and-executive-management/)

## The departures were the real board reset

The AGM notice made the turnover explicit. Tomas Duffy was retiring from the board. Erik Fällström and Keith Halsey were leaving it. The current board page showed Duffy had been elected in 2016, Fällström in 2017 and Halsey in 2024. Whatever the personal reasons, the effect was to strip out three directors associated with earlier chapters of the company and replace them with a smaller, more transaction-ready slate. [AGM notice](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/notice-to-attend-the-annual-general-meeting-of-sivers-semiconductors-ab-publ-6/), [board page](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/investors/corporate-governance/board-of-directors-and-executive-management/)

## The incoming slate

The nomination committee proposed Joakim Nideborn and Helena Svancar as new directors, with Nideborn also proposed as vice chairman. Sivers said Nideborn would take primary board oversight for customers, employees and investors in the Nordic region. HMS Networks' management page identified him as CFO since December 2017 and deputy CEO since January 2022. Sivers described Svancar as bringing more than 20 years of international leadership experience in corporate strategy, governance, cross-border M&A and capital markets; Verdane's profile said she had been head of M&A at Ericsson for almost five years and, before that, spent a decade at Deutsche Bank, including as managing director and head of corporate finance Nordics. [board nominations](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-welcomes-the-nomination-of-new-board-members-joakim-nideborn-and-helena-svancar/), [HMS Networks management](https://www.hms-networks.com/about-hms/management), [Verdane profile](https://verdane.com/team/helena-svancar/)

## The board after the AGM proposal

If shareholders approved the slate exactly as proposed, the board would number five directors: Bastani, Raj, Thomson, Nideborn and Svancar. The CEO was not a proposed director. That was a more compact and more obviously US-facing structure than the one it replaced, with operating depth, capital-markets experience and M&A expertise all concentrated more heavily than before. [AGM notice](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/notice-to-attend-the-annual-general-meeting-of-sivers-semiconductors-ab-publ-6/)

## Overhang

The governance overhang at the snapshot date was therefore less about personalities than about timing. On 13 May 2026, Sivers postponed the Q1 2026 report from 20 May to 29 May as part of the ongoing PCAOB uplift. The AGM notice that followed then asked shareholders not only to elect the new board but also to authorise up to 53,844,956 new ordinary shares. The board refresh and the financing authority were part of the same package. [annual report release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/), [AGM notice](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/notice-to-attend-the-annual-general-meeting-of-sivers-semiconductors-ab-publ-6/)

chapters.title: Where Sivers sits in the AI photonics stack
chapters.body:
# Where Sivers sits in the AI photonics stack

## The layer that did not ship to hyperscalers directly

Investors often spoke about Sivers as though it had a direct route into hyperscaler procurement. The company's own disclosures pointed to something narrower. Sivers Photonics sat beneath the optical-engine and module integrators: it designed and manufactured the DFB laser arrays and related photonic components that its partners then built into external light sources, optical engines or optical-I/O systems.

That distinction mattered because it made Sivers a supplier to the design layer rather than to Microsoft, Meta, Google or AWS themselves. The revenue question was therefore not whether hyperscaler capex was real — it clearly was — but which of Sivers' direct counterparties would win the optical slot one layer above. [2025 annual report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/)

## POET: the clearest named ELS partnership

The most explicit external-light-source relationship in the public record was POET. On 29 September 2025, POET said it had entered a strategic collaboration with Sivers to develop high-performance, cost-effective ELS modules for co-packaged optics and next-generation AI infrastructure. POET said the arrangement paired Sivers' high-power DFB lasers with POET's Optical Interposer platform. When Sivers revisited the partnership on 6 November 2025, it added timing: customer prototypes in the first half of 2026, production readiness targeted by the end of 2026. [POET collaboration announcement](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-sivers-semiconductors-collaborate-on-external-light-sources-for-co-packaged-optics-and-next-generation-ai-market), [Sivers follow-up release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-partners-with-poet-technologies-to-deliver-innovative-light-engines-and-strengthen-serviceable-market-offerings-in-next-gen-ai-infrastructure/)

That was why POET mattered disproportionately. It was not merely another logo; it was the only public relationship that tied Sivers' lasers to a clearly described ELS product roadmap and a published 2026 prototype-to-production sequence.

## Ayar Labs: the longer relationship

The Ayar Labs relationship was older and, in some respects, more technically mature. Sivers disclosed work on CW-WDM MSA-compliant DFB arrays for Ayar as early as 2021. In September 2022 it said its laser arrays had been demonstrated live with Ayar's SuperNova light source at ECOC. In July 2023 it announced a further USD 1 million order from Ayar for light-source technology, saying the arrays would support Ayar's SuperNova remote optical source as it scaled toward volume production. In December 2024, Sivers said it was in advanced discussions with Ayar on the next phase of engagement, focused on product qualification, manufacturing readiness, NRE and product pre-purchases for higher-volume deployment. [CW-WDM array development](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-to-develop-cw-wdm-msa-compliant-dfb-laser-arrays/), [ECOC 2022 demonstration](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-photonics-och-ayar-labs-demonstrerar-supernova-ljuskalla-med-flera-vaglangder-med-sivers-dfb-lasermatriser-vid-ecoc-2022/), [Ayar order](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-photonics-receives-new-order-worth-1m-from-ayar-labs-for-light-source-technology-to-support-the-growth-of-generative-ai/), [Ayar expansion](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-and-ayar-labs-to-expand-their-partnership-on-enabling-high-volume-manufacturing-of-optical-i-o-solutions-for-scalable-cost-effective-ai-infrastructure/)

Ayar therefore looked less like a one-off announcement and more like a multi-stage engineering relationship that had moved from platform development into manufacturing preparation.

## O-Net and Enablence: the serviceability and thermal case

Sivers' O-Net relationship first became public on 1 April 2025, when the companies said O-Net would serve as an OEM partner integrating Sivers' DFB laser arrays into O-Net's external-laser small-form-factor optical modules. On 17 March 2026, Sivers expanded that architecture by adding Enablence and its NxN star coupler, describing a three-way effort to build an advanced ELS module for AI datacenters and HPC systems. Sivers' own explanation of the architecture was revealing: ELS mattered because it kept temperature-sensitive lasers away from the extreme heat of high-power processors, improving wavelength stability, reliability and serviceability. [O-Net OEM partnership](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-announces-strategic-oem-partnership-with-o-net-technologies-to-deliver-next-generation-external-laser-sources-for-co-packaged-optics/), [O-Net/Enablence release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-o-net-and-enablence-technologies-announce-external-light-sources-for-ai-datacenters/)

## imec: the structural endorsement

Sivers' relationship with imec mattered because it pre-dated the current AI-euphoria cycle. In June 2021, Sivers Photonics, imec and ASM AMICRA said they had demonstrated hybrid integration of Sivers' indium-phosphide DFB lasers onto silicon-photonics circuits using wafer-scale flip-chip bonding. That was not the same thing as a hyperscaler order, but it was a meaningful third-party validation of the company's technical relevance inside silicon-photonics ecosystems. [imec collaboration](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-photonics-joins-forces-with-imec-and-asm-amicra-to-accelerate-hybrid-integration-of-silicon-photonics/)

## The wireless and LiDAR side paths

The wireless business sat in a different part of the stack entirely, with named programmes at ESA, Intelsat and NEMC. The largest single disclosed photonics revenue opportunity outside AI interconnects was the unnamed LiDAR customer announced in March 2026. Sivers said that relationship covered lasers and optical amplifiers, with a Q4 2026 production ramp target and lifecycle revenue potential of USD 53 million to USD 138 million. [ESA contract](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-awarded-european-space-agency-contract-for-next-generation-satcom-beamforming-ics/), [Intelsat contract](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-wins-intelsat-satcom-digitizer-development-program-award/), [NEMC Year 2 funding](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/microelectronics-commons-strengthens-commitment-to-sivers-semiconductors-with-year-2-funding/), [LiDAR customer release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/strategic-lidar-customer-ramps-remote-sensing-production-with-sivers-semiconductors-technology/)

## The pipeline caveat

The attraction of the AI-photonics story was that Sivers' named partners were real and its role in the chain was technically intelligible. The limitation was that most of those partners were themselves still in the qualification, prototype or manufacturing-readiness phase. POET had a public end-2026 production-readiness target. Ayar was talking about high-volume deployment in the next 18 to 24 months. O-Net and Enablence were still at the module-development stage. The LiDAR ramp was also still projected rather than realised. [POET collaboration announcement](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-sivers-semiconductors-collaborate-on-external-light-sources-for-co-packaged-optics-and-next-generation-ai-market), [Ayar expansion](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-and-ayar-labs-to-expand-their-partnership-on-enabling-high-volume-manufacturing-of-optical-i-o-solutions-for-scalable-cost-effective-ai-infrastructure/), [O-Net/Enablence release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-o-net-and-enablence-technologies-announce-external-light-sources-for-ai-datacenters/), [LiDAR customer release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/strategic-lidar-customer-ramps-remote-sensing-production-with-sivers-semiconductors-technology/)

## The validation test

By 23 May 2026, no hyperscaler or GPU vendor had publicly named Sivers as a production supplier. The company's position was therefore best understood as technically credible but commercially indirect: it was sitting in the right layer of the stack, but success still depended on someone one step above converting design work into shipped volume.

chapters.title: Why the comparison is COHR and LITE, but the analog is something smaller
chapters.body:
# Why the comparison is COHR and LITE, but the analog is something smaller

## The scale gap was real

The instinct to benchmark Sivers against Coherent and Lumentum was understandable because those were the large listed optical-component groups already selling into AI datacenters. Their own public filings showed the scale mismatch clearly. Coherent reported fiscal 2025 revenue of USD 5.81 billion, Lumentum reported fiscal 2025 revenue of USD 1.65 billion, and MACOM reported fiscal 2025 revenue of USD 967.3 million. Sivers, by contrast, reported FY2025 net sales of SEK 306.6 million. [Coherent FY2025 results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/820318/000119312525179833/d22249dex991.htm), [Lumentum FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx), [MACOM FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1493594/000149359425000054/mtsi-20251003.htm), [Sivers 2025 annual report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/)

That did not make the comparison useless. It changed what the comparison meant. Sivers was not trying to replicate the broad transceiver, subsystem and industrial-photonics portfolios of Coherent or Lumentum. It was trying to occupy a narrower layer: the custom DFB-laser and external-light-source position inside emerging CPO architectures.

## What changed at the CPO layer

In traditional pluggables, laser supply had long since been partly standardised. In CPO and advanced ELS modules, the Sivers argument was that customisation mattered more: wavelength-stable CW lasers, thermal separation from the processor package, and integration to a specific interposer or module design. That was the commercial logic behind the company's public sequence with [POET](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-sivers-semiconductors-collaborate-on-external-light-sources-for-co-packaged-optics-and-next-generation-ai-market), [Ayar Labs](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-and-ayar-labs-to-expand-their-partnership-on-enabling-high-volume-manufacturing-of-optical-i-o-solutions-for-scalable-cost-effective-ai-infrastructure/), [O-Net](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-announces-strategic-oem-partnership-with-o-net-technologies-to-deliver-next-generation-external-laser-sources-for-co-packaged-optics/) and [O-Net/Enablence](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-o-net-and-enablence-technologies-announce-external-light-sources-for-ai-datacenters/).

The company was not claiming to own the full optical stack. It was trying to become hard to replace at a single upstream point inside it.

## The counterargument had substance

The incumbents were not standing still. Coherent said in March 2026 that it was ramping 6-inch InP production across its fabs and highlighted its own CPO-oriented CW-laser and external-light-source products. Lumentum, also in March 2026, announced plans for a new Greensboro facility to manufacture InP-based optical products, including CW and ultra-high-power lasers for AI datacenters. [Coherent InP release](https://www.coherent.com/news/press-releases/coherent-demonstrates-inp-technology-innovation), [Lumentum Greensboro facility](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-New-U-S--Manufacturing-Facility-to-Produce-Advanced-Lasers-for-the-Worlds-Largest-AI-Data-Centers/default.aspx)

That mattered because the bullish Sivers case relied on scarcity. Every announced expansion by a vertically integrated incumbent shortened the period in which a smaller independent supplier could turn design wins into something closer to a chokepoint.

## The more useful analog

MACOM was the closer strategic analog, not because it was the same size, but because it too sold components into optical systems rather than owning the entire module stack. MACOM's 2025 revenue was almost USD 1 billion and its group operating margin was 13.4 per cent. Sivers, by contrast, finished FY2025 with SEK 306.6 million of revenue and an EBIT margin of roughly negative 58 per cent. The gap was not cosmetic. It described a company still in the investment-and-qualification stage rather than in scaled component economics. [MACOM FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1493594/000149359425000054/mtsi-20251003.htm), [Sivers 2025 annual report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/)

## Geography as a variable

What Sivers did have that was harder to model was geography. The ESA award, the Intelsat digitizer programme and the NEMC-funded defence work all pointed to customers that cared about traceable Western supply in at least part of the business. If AI optical interconnect buyers reached a similar conclusion about indium-phosphide lasers, Sivers' Scottish fab and European domicile could matter more than a conventional model would capture. But that remained strategic possibility rather than booked-order fact as of 23 May 2026. [ESA contract](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-awarded-european-space-agency-contract-for-next-generation-satcom-beamforming-ics/), [Intelsat contract](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-wins-intelsat-satcom-digitizer-development-program-award/), [NEMC Year 2 funding](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/microelectronics-commons-strengthens-commitment-to-sivers-semiconductors-with-year-2-funding/)

## What the market was really betting on

The market was not paying for Sivers as it existed in 2025. It was paying for the possibility that one of the named design-house relationships — POET, Ayar Labs, or O-Net/Enablence — would convert the company from a development supplier into a production supplier before the large incumbents made that upstream niche less scarce. That was why the more relevant question was not whether Sivers could become another Coherent. It was whether it could lock in one valuable production slot before Coherent, Lumentum and other integrated players absorbed the same layer themselves.

# Twelve months of headlines — and how the equity story has travelled

## The leadership shift that reframed the company

The change that mattered first was managerial. Vickram Vathulya's appointment, effective 19 August 2024, marked the start of a more explicit US-facing commercial narrative around AI photonics and co-packaged optics. The market did not reprice the stock on that appointment alone, but it changed the script management would use for the next year. [CEO appointment](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-appoints-vickram-vathulya-as-new-president-ceo/)

## The POET partnership and the rerating

The headline that most clearly shifted the equity story came from POET on 29 September 2025. POET said it had entered a strategic collaboration with Sivers to build external light sources for co-packaged optics and next-generation AI infrastructure. Sivers' own 6 November follow-up then made the timetable more explicit by pointing to customer prototypes in the first half of 2026 and production readiness by the end of 2026. That was enough for specialist investors to start treating Sivers less as a mixed Swedish small-cap and more as an upstream option on the AI optical-interconnect buildout. [POET collaboration announcement](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-sivers-semiconductors-collaborate-on-external-light-sources-for-co-packaged-optics-and-next-generation-ai-market), [Sivers follow-up release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-partners-with-poet-technologies-to-deliver-innovative-light-engines-and-strengthen-serviceable-market-offerings-in-next-gen-ai-infrastructure/)

## February 2026: refinancing and preliminary momentum

On 24 February 2026, Sivers refinanced its external debt with Bootstrap Europe. On 26 February, it published the Q4 2025 year-end report showing annual net sales of SEK 304.1 million on the pre-restatement basis, Q4 net sales of SEK 80.7 million and a year-end pipeline of USD 453 million. Those two releases worked together: the refinancing addressed survival, and the year-end report preserved the growth story. [Bootstrap refinancing](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-refinances-group-debt-facilities-with-bootstrap-europe-to-strengthen-capital-structure/), [Q4 2025 interim report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Sivers-Interim-report-Q425_Final.pdf)

## May 2026: accounting, grants and governance

The heavier reckoning came on 13 May 2026, when Sivers published its PCAOB-restated annual report and simultaneously postponed the Q1 2026 report from 20 May to 29 May. Six days later, it announced the USD 6.6 million NEMC Year 2 extension. On 20 May, it followed with the nomination of Joakim Nideborn and Helena Svancar to a new five-person board slate for the 15 June AGM. By the snapshot date, the public news flow had clearly converged on one theme: Sivers was rearranging both its accounts and its governance for a possible US listing. [annual report release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/), [NEMC Year 2 funding](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/microelectronics-commons-strengthens-commitment-to-sivers-semiconductors-with-year-2-funding/), [board nominations](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-welcomes-the-nomination-of-new-board-members-joakim-nideborn-and-helena-svancar/)

Forward catalysts within 90 to 180 days were therefore concrete rather than speculative: the delayed Q1 2026 report, the 15 June AGM, any formal step in the Nasdaq New York process, the POET prototype timetable, and the unnamed LiDAR customer's targeted Q4 2026 production ramp. [LiDAR customer release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/strategic-lidar-customer-ramps-remote-sensing-production-with-sivers-semiconductors-technology/)

## How the equity story travelled in commentary

Specialist commentary did not need to invent a narrative; the company had supplied one. Sivers had spent late 2025 and early 2026 naming counterparties across POET, Ayar, O-Net, Enablence, ESA, Intelsat and NEMC. The bullish interpretation was straightforward: Sivers was not yet booking hyperscaler-scale revenue, but it had inserted itself into several places where a small photonics supplier could matter disproportionately if CPO architectures moved from demonstrations to production.

That remained the key limitation as well. The public record by 23 May 2026 still showed partnerships, qualification work, funded development and roadmap language rather than a named hyperscaler production order. The equity story had travelled a long way; the order book had not caught up with the share price.

chapters.title: InP DFB lasers — patents, products, and the case for chokepoint pricing
chapters.body:
# InP DFB lasers — patents, products, and the case for chokepoint pricing

The IP-density question was the right place to start. If Sivers held a genuine chokepoint, it could command pricing power and customer stickiness. If not, it was simply a capable specialist fabricator benefiting from a timely market narrative.

Sivers' own disclosures described the moat less as a giant patent wall than as a blend of narrow patenting and accumulated process knowledge. In the August 2024 byNordic LOI materials, Sivers said the photonics unit had three issued patents and 16 pending applications across the US, UK, Canada and WIPO. In the October 2024 Photonics-AI presentation, the company refined the language further: its IP strategy was based on 25 years of proprietary know-how and trade secrets, with three patents granted in the prior three years and 16 patents pending from the prior two years. [byNordic LOI](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-enters-into-letter-of-intent-with-bynordic-acquisition-corporation-for-business-combination-of-sivers-photonics-subsidiary/), [Photonics-AI presentation](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Sivers-Photonics.pdf)

That was a more defensible formulation than simply counting patents in isolation. The company's own materials were effectively saying that the patent portfolio existed, but that the deeper asset was embedded in fabrication recipes, epi-wafer design, laser design, testing methodology and custom in-house software. [Photonics-AI presentation](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Sivers-Photonics.pdf)

## The three-layer technical stack

The chokepoint was not a single component. It was the ability to execute across three technical layers at once.

First came III-V epitaxial growth. High-power indium-phosphide devices still depended on tight process control at the wafer level. Second came DFB grating design and fabrication, which determined whether a laser array would hold the wavelength stability and power characteristics demanded by silicon-photonics systems. Third came hybrid integration with the downstream silicon-photonics platform or external-light-source package.

That third layer was where outside validation appeared. In June 2021, Sivers Photonics, imec and ASM AMICRA said they had demonstrated hybrid integration of indium-phosphide DFB lasers onto silicon-photonics circuits using wafer-scale flip-chip bonding. That did not prove a mass-market franchise, but it showed Sivers was building at the right technical frontier for advanced optical I/O. [imec collaboration](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-photonics-joins-forces-with-imec-and-asm-amicra-to-accelerate-hybrid-integration-of-silicon-photonics/)

## Where the patents did not tell the whole story

The October 2024 photonics deck all but said openly that patents were not the entire story. It highlighted trade secrets built over 25 years, in-house design capability and manufacturing know-how as the core differentiation moat. That was consistent with how specialist semiconductor-process businesses usually protect value: patent the most obvious high-impact concepts, keep the most commercially sensitive process steps inside the fab. [Photonics-AI presentation](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Sivers-Photonics.pdf)

The counterargument was obvious as well. A trade-secret moat was real only as long as the engineering organisation, process control and customer intimacy stayed intact. A larger rival with money and patience could still build or buy a competing capability.

## R&D intensity, obscured by the accounting uplift

The restated annual report did not present the story as a clean, software-like R&D line item. Instead, the most important disclosure was the opposite: one of the PCAOB uplift drivers was impairment of previously capitalised development expenditure. That meant the company had been investing heavily enough in development that the accounting treatment itself became material to the equity story. [2025 annual report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/)

## The margin horizon

Whether that process and IP investment would earn attractive returns depended on scale. MACOM, a far more mature component supplier, reported fiscal 2025 revenue of USD 967.3 million and group operating income margin of 13.4 per cent. Sivers, by contrast, reported FY2025 revenue of SEK 306.6 million and EBIT margin of roughly negative 58 per cent. The distance between those two states was not incremental; it required actual production ramps. [MACOM FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1493594/000149359425000054/mtsi-20251003.htm), [Sivers 2025 annual report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/)

The May 2026 continuation of the NEMC programme did at least suggest technical milestones were being met on the defence side. Sivers said the USD 6.6 million Year 2 extension reflected strong first-year technical progress and milestone execution. That was only a sliver of validation, but it was still validation. [NEMC Year 2 funding](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/microelectronics-commons-strengthens-commitment-to-sivers-semiconductors-with-year-2-funding/)

The right way to think about the moat, then, was not as a raw patent count. It was as a combination of proprietary laser-process know-how, hybrid-integration capability, and customer-specific development work that could become sticky if partners moved into volume. The next two years would decide whether that remained a technical lead or hardened into commercial leverage.

chapters.title: What could break this
chapters.body:
# What could break this

The bull case rested on a sequence: named development programmes had to turn into production ramps, the USD 453 million pipeline had to start converting into recognised revenue, and the company had to fund the gap without letting dilution outrun operating progress. Break any link in that chain and the timing of breakeven moved sharply to the right.

## The calendar problem

Both of the most important photonics milestones were still ahead as of the frozen date. POET's September and November 2025 disclosures pointed to customer prototypes in the first half of 2026 and production readiness by the end of 2026. The unnamed LiDAR customer disclosed in March 2026 pointed to a production ramp from Q4 2026. Neither milestone had yet been validated by shipment. [POET collaboration announcement](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-sivers-semiconductors-collaborate-on-external-light-sources-for-co-packaged-optics-and-next-generation-ai-market), [Sivers follow-up release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-partners-with-poet-technologies-to-deliver-innovative-light-engines-and-strengthen-serviceable-market-offerings-in-next-gen-ai-infrastructure/), [LiDAR customer release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/strategic-lidar-customer-ramps-remote-sensing-production-with-sivers-semiconductors-technology/)

Semiconductor ramps did not usually arrive exactly on first-announced timelines. A two-quarter slip in either POET or LiDAR would matter not just for revenue timing but for the financing path that sat in between.

## The runway equation

The restated annual report showed cash and cash equivalents of SEK 43.5 million at year-end 2025. Net cash flow from operating activities before changes in working capital was negative SEK 64.8 million. The Bootstrap package improved that position, but it also added leverage and a convertible overhang: USD 5 million of term debt at 12 per cent and USD 12 million of convertible debt at 10.85 per cent, convertible at SEK 4.77. [2025 annual report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/), [Bootstrap refinancing](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-refinances-group-debt-facilities-with-bootstrap-europe-to-strengthen-capital-structure/)

The 15 June 2026 AGM notice then asked shareholders to authorise up to 53,844,956 new ordinary shares. Boards asked for that degree of flexibility when they expected to need it. [AGM notice](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/notice-to-attend-the-annual-general-meeting-of-sivers-semiconductors-ab-publ-6/)

## A pipeline was not a backlog

The USD 453 million pipeline was the most repeated commercial number in the dossier, and it was plainly important. But the named public counterparties around that pipeline — POET, Ayar Labs, O-Net/Enablence and the unnamed LiDAR customer — were mostly still in stages described as collaboration, development, qualification, manufacturing readiness or ramp planning. That was not the same thing as a booked backlog. [Q4 2025 interim report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Sivers-Interim-report-Q425_Final.pdf), [POET collaboration announcement](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-sivers-semiconductors-collaborate-on-external-light-sources-for-co-packaged-optics-and-next-generation-ai-market), [Ayar expansion](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-and-ayar-labs-to-expand-their-partnership-on-enabling-high-volume-manufacturing-of-optical-i-o-solutions-for-scalable-cost-effective-ai-infrastructure/), [O-Net/Enablence release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-o-net-and-enablence-technologies-announce-external-light-sources-for-ai-datacenters/), [LiDAR customer release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/strategic-lidar-customer-ramps-remote-sensing-production-with-sivers-semiconductors-technology/)

If one or more of those design positions slipped, the market would discover very quickly how much of the valuation was forward-dated.

## The chokepoint could narrow before it monetised

The strategic argument also depended on timing relative to larger incumbents. Coherent said in March 2026 that it was ramping 6-inch InP production across multiple fabs and highlighted its own CPO-oriented CW-laser and ELS products. Lumentum, in the same month, announced a new Greensboro manufacturing site for InP-based CW and ultra-high-power lasers for AI datacenters. Those were precisely the categories Sivers was trying to make scarce. [Coherent InP release](https://www.coherent.com/news/press-releases/coherent-demonstrates-inp-technology-innovation), [Lumentum Greensboro facility](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-New-U-S--Manufacturing-Facility-to-Produce-Advanced-Lasers-for-the-Worlds-Largest-AI-Data-Centers/default.aspx)

Sivers did not need to outbuild those companies. It needed to win enough early positions before they made the same upstream niche less differentiated.

## What the restatement signalled

The PCAOB uplift was analytically useful because it made the accounting more conservative. It also carried process risk. The same 13 May 2026 release that published the annual report postponed the Q1 2026 report to 29 May because the audit uplift work was still under way. If the listing process remained open-ended, investors were being asked to fund a company whose operational milestones and reporting transition were happening in parallel. [annual report release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/)

## Currency and mix still mattered

Finally, the company remained exposed to factors that could blur the headline growth story. Q4 2025 net sales rose 5 per cent on a reported basis but 17 per cent in constant currency, showing how much translation effects could distort the trend line. And even after all the excitement around photonics, the restated annual report still showed Wireless generating SEK 213.1 million of revenue in 2025 against Photonics' SEK 93.4 million. The valuation was being driven by the smaller division. [Q4 2025 interim report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Sivers-Interim-report-Q425_Final.pdf), [2025 annual report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/)

chapters.title: Three events that will decide whether the rally was right
chapters.body:
# Three events that will decide whether the rally was right

## The vote that cleared the table

On 15 June 2026, Sivers shareholders were due to vote on a board and capital package designed to prepare the company for its next phase. The nomination committee proposed a five-person board comprising returning directors Bami Bastani, Karin Raj and Todd Thomson, plus new nominees Joakim Nideborn and Helena Svancar, with Nideborn also proposed as vice chairman. The same AGM notice asked shareholders to authorise issues of up to 53,844,956 new ordinary shares and said that mandate could also be used to facilitate a potential Nasdaq New York dual listing. [AGM notice](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/notice-to-attend-the-annual-general-meeting-of-sivers-semiconductors-ab-publ-6/), [board nominations](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-welcomes-the-nomination-of-new-board-members-joakim-nideborn-and-helena-svancar/)

The significance of that meeting was not whether the resolutions would probably pass. It was that the board refresh and the financing flexibility were being presented as parts of the same transition.

## The module that had to ship

The POET partnership remained the cleanest single embodiment of the photonics bull case. POET's September 2025 announcement created the collaboration; Sivers' November 2025 update put prototypes in the first half of 2026 and production readiness at year-end 2026. In parallel, the unnamed LiDAR customer pointed to a Q4 2026 production ramp. Those were the operational gates that mattered most. [POET collaboration announcement](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-sivers-semiconductors-collaborate-on-external-light-sources-for-co-packaged-optics-and-next-generation-ai-market), [Sivers follow-up release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-partners-with-poet-technologies-to-deliver-innovative-light-engines-and-strengthen-serviceable-market-offerings-in-next-gen-ai-infrastructure/), [LiDAR customer release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/strategic-lidar-customer-ramps-remote-sensing-production-with-sivers-semiconductors-technology/)

What the public timeline could not answer was whether yields, reliability testing and customer qualification would keep up with the calendar. A successful production launch would validate the upstream-laser thesis quickly. A material delay would send the company back toward the capital markets before the thesis had been proven.

## The price that set the ceiling

The accounting uplift was a prerequisite, not an outcome. The April 2026 dual-listing evaluation announcement, the May 2026 restated annual report, the postponed Q1 report and the AGM issuance authority all made clear that Sivers was still building the bridge to a US capital-markets event rather than walking across it. [dual-listing evaluation](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-ab-evaluates-a-potential-dual-listing-of-its-shares-on-the-nasdaq-new-york/), [annual report release](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/)

At SEK 72.90 on 22 May 2026, using the AGM notice's ordinary-share count net of treasury stock, the market valued Sivers at roughly SEK 22.2 billion against FY2025 restated revenue of SEK 306.6 million, or about 72 times trailing sales. That valuation left little room for an equity raise that implied a very different assessment of the business. [share-price widget](https://widget.datablocks.se/api/rose/widgets/stock-chart?token=01434696-043a-4b12-8609-959b0f82e6a0&lang=en), [AGM notice](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/notice-to-attend-the-annual-general-meeting-of-sivers-semiconductors-ab-publ-6/), [2025 annual report](https://www.sivers-semiconductors.com/press/sivers-semiconductors-publishes-the-2025-annual-report-adjusting-prior-reported-financials-as-preparation-for-a-potential-dual-listing-in-the-united-states/)

The practical test, then, was simple. If Sivers could move from partnership language to production evidence while accessing capital on terms that respected the Stockholm valuation, the rally would look prescient. If it needed to raise money before those ramps were validated, the market would be forced to decide how much of the story it really wanted to underwrite.

The next 18 months were still going to determine whether the chokepoint was real. But by 23 May 2026, the market had already priced as though the answer would eventually be yes.

The tables and reference materials that follow are organised to let readers pressure-test the arguments made in the preceding chapters against the underlying numbers and primary sources.

## Financial Tables

The financial appendix presents three years of income-statement and balance-sheet data in parallel columns — Swedish K3 as filed and PCAOB-restated — so the SEK 36.5M gap in FY2025 EBIT (–141.3M reported vs. –177.8M restated) and the FY2024 revenue compression (243.7M → 219.2M) are visible at a glance alongside the five restatement drivers.

## Leadership Graph

The leadership appendix maps board tenure, departure dates, and the professional lineage connecting Vickram Vathulya, Bami Bastani, and the incoming AGM nominees — tracing the organisational logic of the US-listing preparation from the August 2023 strategic advisor appointment through the June 2026 board reshuffle.

## Counterparty Map

The counterparty appendix organises named partners, named customers, implied indirect customers, and creditors into a single reference table, with segment, scope, and confirmation status flagged for each relationship.

## Press Release Index

Chronological index of material company announcements from 2023 through the snapshot date, with direct links.

## Aleabit Primary-Source Notes

Raw excerpts and commentary from the Aleabit research thread that surfaced several claims — including the Apple/SiPH reference — not yet confirmed in official Sivers filings. Treat as unverified leads.
